chapter_title: AI Agents, Prompts, and Rubric Scoring
learning_objective: The learner will classify each of ten sentences from prompts under the prompt part it belongs to, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** prompt-part-sorter
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify each of ten sentences from prompts under the prompt part it belongs to, with at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Prompt (defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each sentence the learner commits one of six parts. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct part column in Content. Mastery is at least 9 of 10 correct on the first attempt. Reading the part definitions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Anything phrased as a command is the task. (2) A rule and an output format are the same. (3) An example is part of the input. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying sentences by their job in a prompt is an Understand-level action that prepares the learner to write and revise prompts. Ten sentences that cover each part show the learner what each part sounds like. **Content:** The six parts: Role, Task, Input, Rules, Output format, Example. The ten sentences: | # | Sentence shown to the learner | Correct part | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | You are a careful reviewer of open educational resources. | Role | It says who the model should act as. | | 2 | Score the resource on the accessibility metric from 0 to 10. | Task | It names the action to perform. | | 3 | Here is the resource: {{resource_text}} | Input | It supplies the material, with a slot for the text. | | 4 | Give a result only for checks you can verify from the text, and otherwise write "not checkable". | Rules | It says what to do when unsure. | | 5 | Return a table with one row per check and the columns check, result, and evidence. | Output format | It shapes the answer. | | 6 | Example: Check 1: Fail. Evidence: 4 of 5 images have alt text (page 3). | Example | It shows a sample answer. | | 7 | Never invent a quotation or a page number. | Rules | It forbids a behavior. | | 8 | Act as an experienced instructional designer. | Role | It says who the model should act as. | | 9 | List every image on the page and say whether it has alt text. | Task | It names the action to perform. | | 10 | Respond only in JSON with the keys metric, score, and evidence. | Output format | It shapes the answer. | **Provenance:** The sentences are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The parts follow the chapter section "Prompt". **Rules:** Each sentence has exactly one correct part. Two sentences are Role, two are Task, one is Input, two are Rules, two are Output format, and one is Example. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one sentence and the six parts. 2. The learner may open the part definitions. Opening them does not change the score. 3. The learner places the sentence under a part, and the placement is committed. 4. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 5. After sentence 10 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 10 sentences in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [part]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This is [part]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 10 correct on the first attempt". At 9 or more it adds "You can hear the parts of a prompt." Below 9 it lists the Why text of each missed sentence. **Starting State:** The first sentence and the six parts. The question shown is "Which part of a prompt is this sentence?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter lists the six parts as role, task, input, rules, output format, and example.
